The purpose of this script is to validate the three datasets used in the Atlantic bluefin tuna project: the DFO Fisheries Atlas, GEBCO 2026 bathymetry and Copernicus GLORYS oceanography. Here, I confirm their suitability by inspecting their layers and variables, CRS, extent, resolution and time coverage. No environmental extraction, statistical analysis or final figure production is performed here.  

# Setup
```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE
)

# Load necessary packages
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(here)
library(tibble)
library(terra)
library(purrr)
```

# DFO Fisheries Atlas Validation

```{r inspect-fisheries-geodatabase}
# Define the location of the original fisheries geodatabase
fisheries_geodatabase_path <- here(
  "data",
  "raw_data",
  "DFO_FisheriesAtlas",
  "Maritimes_Fisheries_Atlas_2019_2023.gdb"
)

# Inspect available spatial layers without importing every layer
fisheries_layer_information <- st_layers(
  fisheries_geodatabase_path
)

# Create a summary of the original geodatabase contents.
fisheries_layer_summary <- tibble(
  layer_name = fisheries_layer_information$name,
  geometry_type = vapply(     
    # vapply converts geometry descriptions to a text column
    fisheries_layer_information$geomtype,
    paste,
    collapse = ", ",
    FUN.VALUE = character(1)
  ),
  feature_count = fisheries_layer_information$features
)

# Display all available layers (not just the shortened tibble output)
print(fisheries_layer_summary, n = Inf)
```

## Biological Data Inspection
Eight fisheries layers were selected in total. A bluefin tuna layer and seven comparison fisheries; their attributes and spatial properties will also be checked before processing.

```{r inspect-biological-data}

# Identify the fishery layers for species of interest:
selected_species_layers <- c(
  bluefin_tuna = "BluefinTuna_Landings_Weight_2019_2023",
  atlantic_herring = "Herring_Landings_Weight_2019_2023",
  atlantic_mackerel = "Mackerel_Landings_Weight_2019_2023",
  squid = "Squid_Landings_Weight_2019_2023",
  whitehake = "WhiteHake_Landings_Weight_2019_2023",
  silverhake = "SilverHake_Landings_Weight_2019_2023",
  redhake = "RedHake_Landings_Weight_2019_2023",
  cusk = "Cusk_Landings_Weight_2019_2023"
)

# Import selected fishery layers using lapply () for efficiency
fisheries_species_data <- lapply(
  selected_species_layers,
  function(layer_name) {
    st_read(
      dsn = fisheries_geodatabase_path,
      layer = layer_name,
      quiet = TRUE
    )
  }
)

# Inspect column names for each species
species_attribute_summary <- lapply(
  fisheries_species_data,
  names
)

species_attribute_summary # This will print the column names for each species layer, allowing me to verify that the necessary attributes are present for further analysis.

# Preview bluefin tuna records
head(fisheries_species_data$bluefin_tuna)

```

The later scripts use 'hexGridID' to match reporting cells and `roundWeight_kg` to analyse reported catch weight.

```{r}
# Check fields required for fisheries processing
required_fisheries_fields <- c(
  "hexGridID",
  "roundWeight_kg"
)

fisheries_field_validation <- purrr::imap_dfr(
  fisheries_species_data,
  function(species_data, species_name) {

    attributes <- sf::st_drop_geometry(species_data)

    tibble::tibble(
      species = species_name,
      
      missing_fields = paste(
        setdiff(required_fisheries_fields, names(attributes)),
        collapse = ", "
      ),

      missing_grid_ids = if ("hexGridID" %in% names(attributes)) {
        sum(is.na(attributes$hexGridID))
      } else {
        NA_integer_
      },
# Return NA if the field does not exist
      missing_catch_weights = if ("roundWeight_kg" %in% names(attributes)) {
        sum(is.na(attributes$roundWeight_kg))
      } else {
        NA_integer_
      }
    )
  }
)

print(fisheries_field_validation, n = Inf)
```

The fisheries layers are checked for coorindate systems/geometry validtity and missing values / geograpic extent. 

## Fisheries Data Validation

```{r validate-fisheries-data}

# Check spatial properties and missing values
fisheries_compatibility_summary <- purrr::imap_dfr(
  fisheries_species_data,
  function(species_data, species_name) {

    geographic_extent <- st_bbox(
      st_transform(species_data, 4326) # Transform coordinates to WGS84 for consistent geographic extent calculation (does not change original layer CRS)
    )

    tibble(
      species = species_name,
      feature_count = nrow(species_data),
      crs_epsg = st_crs(species_data)$epsg,
      geometry_type = paste(
        unique(as.character(st_geometry_type(species_data))),
        collapse = ", "
      ),
      invalid_geometries = sum(!st_is_valid(species_data), na.rm = TRUE),
      missing_attribute_values = sum(
        is.na(st_drop_geometry(species_data))
      ),
      # Record the geographic extent in decimal degrees (WGS84)
      longitude_min = unname(geographic_extent["xmin"]),
      longitude_max = unname(geographic_extent["xmax"]),
      latitude_min = unname(geographic_extent["ymin"]),
      latitude_max = unname(geographic_extent["ymax"])
    )
  }
)

# Display spatial compatibility
print(fisheries_compatibility_summary, width = Inf)

# Inspect attribute names and data types
fisheries_attribute_summary <- purrr::imap_dfr(
  fisheries_species_data,
  function(species_data, species_name) {

    tibble(
      species = species_name,
      attribute_name = names(st_drop_geometry(species_data)),
      data_type = vapply(
        st_drop_geometry(species_data),
        function(attribute_values) {
          paste(class(attribute_values), collapse = ", ")
        },
        character(1)
      )
    )
  }
)

print(fisheries_attribute_summary, n = Inf)
```
Based on the combined fisheries extents, the environmental-data acquisition area was rounded to 68-55°W and 39-48°N. This extent covers the core fisheries reporting region while keeping raster and NetCDF downloads manageable.

```{r}
# Record the study area extent for future reference which can be used to aquire targetd enviromental data for the fisheries reporting cells.
study_area_extent <- c(
  longitude_min = -68,
  longitude_max = -55,
  latitude_min = 39,
  latitude_max = 48
)
print(study_area_extent)
```

# GEBCO Exploration
GEBCO 2026 bathymetry was downloaded as a GeoTIFF raster for the study area extent. The raster is inspected for spatial properties and elevation/depth values. The data gives seabed elevation which can be used to calculate depth, slope etc. 

```{r}
# Load original raster
gebco_bathymetry <- rast(
  here("data", "raw_data", "GEBCO", "gebco_2026_n48.0_s39.0_w-68.0_e-55.0_geotiff.tif")
)

# Inspect spatial properties
gebco_spatial_summary <- tibble(
  dataset = "GEBCO 2026 Bathymetry",
  coordinate_reference_system = crs(gebco_bathymetry),
  longitude_min = xmin(gebco_bathymetry),
  longitude_max = xmax(gebco_bathymetry),
  latitude_min = ymin(gebco_bathymetry),
  latitude_max = ymax(gebco_bathymetry),
  longitude_resolution = res(gebco_bathymetry)[1],
  latitude_resolution = res(gebco_bathymetry)[2],
  raster_columns = ncol(gebco_bathymetry),
  raster_rows = nrow(gebco_bathymetry),
  missing_cells = global(is.na(gebco_bathymetry), "sum", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1]
)

# Display spatial properties
print(gebco_spatial_summary, width = Inf)

# Inspect elevation and depth values
gebco_depth_summary <- global(
  gebco_bathymetry,
  fun = c("min", "max", "mean"),
  na.rm = TRUE
)

print(gebco_depth_summary)
```
The GEBCO raster covers the preliminary fisheries study area at 15-arc-second resolution and contains no missing raster cells. It is suitable for deriving bathymetric variables for the fisheries reporting cells. 

# Copernicus Data Validation

This dataset provides montlhy oceanographic data which can be used to examine sea surface temperature and currents from 2019-2023. The data is downloaded as a NetCDF file and inspected here. 

```{r inspect-copernicus-data}

# Identify the downloaded NetCDF file
copernicus_file_path <- list.files(
  here("data", "raw_data", "Copernicus"),
  pattern = "\\.nc$",
  full.names = TRUE
)
stopifnot(length(copernicus_file_path) == 1)

# Inspect available variables
copernicus_variables <- terra::sds(copernicus_file_path)

copernicus_variables
```

## Temperature time coverage

```{r validate-copernicus-time}

# Extract monthly timestamps from the temperature dataset
copernicus_temperature <- copernicus_variables["thetao"]

copernicus_time_summary <- tibble(
  first_observation = min(time(copernicus_temperature)),
  last_observation = max(time(copernicus_temperature)),
  number_of_months = nlyr(copernicus_temperature)
)

print(copernicus_time_summary)

```
# Validation Outcome
All datasets were checked and deemed fit for use and comparable for our goal. They have sufficient coverage and spatial extent. The next scripts will process each dataset independently BEFORE integrating environmental variables with the bluefin tuna reporting cells.
